patterns.title: Mo agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don fhocal i ndiaidh mo? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn leabhar ná athair ar an dóigh chéanna?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the word after mo? Why do leabhar and athair not change in the same way?
patterns.rule: Mo puts a h after the first letter (séimhiú): mo dheartháir. L, n and r never take h: mo leabhar. Before a vowel, mo becomes m': m'athair.

patterns.title: I agus urú
patterns.question: Cad chuige a n-athraíonn an litriú i gcuid acu ach nach n-athraíonn sé i gcuid eile?
patterns.questionEn: Why does the spelling change in some of them but not in others?
patterns.rule: I eclipses the next word: i bpuball, i gcarbhán. Before a vowel, i becomes in: in óstán. L, m, n, r and s do not change.

patterns.title: Ar an agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn i ndiaidh ar an i gcanúint Uladh?
patterns.questionEn: What happens after ar an in Ulster Irish?
patterns.rule: In Ulster, ar an puts a h on the next word: ar an bhád, ar an bhus. T, d and vowels do not change: ar an traein, ar an eitleán.

patterns.title: I agus urú le logainmneacha
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn d'ainm na háite i ndiaidh i? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn Ard Mhacha ná Londain ar an dóigh chéanna?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the place name after i? Why do Ard Mhacha and Londain not change in the same way?
patterns.rule: I eclipses the next word: i mBéal Feirste, i gCamloch, i nDoire. Before a vowel, i becomes in: in Ard Mhacha. L, m, n, r and s do not change: i Londain.
patterns.ruleEn: I eclipses the next word: i mBéal Feirste, i gCamloch, i nDoire. Before a vowel, i becomes in: in Ard Mhacha. L, m, n, r and s do not change: i Londain.

patterns.title: Sa agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn i ndiaidh sa? Cad chuige a bhfuil t roimh siopa agus sráid, ach nach n-athraíonn teach?
patterns.questionEn: What happens after sa? Why is there a t before siopa and sráid, but teach does not change?
patterns.rule: Sa means in the. It puts a h after b, c, g, m and p: sa bhaile mór, sa pháirc. Before f, sa becomes san and the f takes a h: san fharraige. Before s followed by a vowel, l, n or r, sa puts a t in front: sa tsiopa, sa tsráid. D and t do not change: sa teach. Before a vowel, sa becomes san: san ionad spóirt.
patterns.ruleEn: Sa means in the. It puts a h after b, c, g, m and p: sa bhaile mór, sa pháirc. Before f, sa becomes san and the f takes a h: san fharraige. patterns.title: An aimsir chaite agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don bhriathar san aimsir chaite? Cad chuige a bhfuil d' roimh chuid acu? Cad é atá aisteach faoi téim?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the verb in the past tense? Why do some of them have d' in front? What is strange about téim?
patterns.rule: In the past tense, put a h after the first letter: bhuail mé, cheannaigh mé. Before a vowel, put d' in front: d'imir mé, d'éirigh mé. F takes both: d'fhan mé. L, n and r do not change: léigh mé. Téigh is irregular: téim becomes chuaigh mé.
patterns.ruleEn: In the past tense, put a h after the first letter: bhuail mé, cheannaigh mé. Before a vowel, put d' in front: d'imir mé, d'éirigh mé. F takes both: d'fhan mé. L, n and r do not change: léigh mé. Téigh is irregular: téim becomes chuaigh mé.

patterns.title: Is maith liom agus ba mhaith liom
patterns.question: Cad é an difear idir is maith liom agus ba mhaith liom? Cad é a tharlaíonn do maith i ndiaidh ba?
patterns.questionEn: What is the difference between is maith liom and ba mhaith liom? What happens to maith after ba?
rows: {Ba} m[h]aith liom an giotár a fhoghlaim.
patterns.rule: Is maith liom means I like, now or in general. Ba mhaith liom means I would like, and an action usually follows it: ba mhaith liom dul ag snámh. Ba puts a h after the next letter: ba mhaith, ba bhreá. Before f or a vowel, ba becomes b': b'fhearr liom. The question and the negative change too: ar mhaith leat? níor mhaith liom.

patterns.title: Uimhreacha agus punt
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don fhocal punt i ndiaidh trí, cúig, seacht agus deich? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn sé i ndiaidh fiche?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the word punt after three, five, seven and ten? Why does it not change after twenty?
patterns.rule: After 2 to 6 the noun takes a h (séimhiú): trí phunt, cúig phunt. After 7 to 10 it is eclipsed (urú): seacht bpunt, deich bpunt. After fiche, tríocha, caoga and the other tens it does not change: fiche punt. The noun stays singular after a number.
patterns.ruleEn: After 2 to 6 the noun takes a h (séimhiú): trí phunt, cúig phunt. After 7 to 10 it is eclipsed (urú): seacht bpunt, deich bpunt. After fiche, tríocha, caoga and the other tens it does not change: fiche punt. The noun stays singular after a number.

patterns.title: Dathanna i ndiaidh an ainmfhocail
patterns.question: Cad chuige a gcuirtear h ar an fhocal bán i ndiaidh léine ach nach gcuirtear i ndiaidh geansaí? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn liath?
patterns.questionEn: Why does bán take a h after léine but not after geansaí? Why does liath not change?
patterns.rule: In Irish the colour comes after the noun. After a feminine noun (léine, casóg, T-léine) the colour takes a h (séimhiú): léine bhán, casóg dhubh. After a masculine noun (geansaí, bríste, cóta) it does not change: geansaí bán. L, n and r never take h: casóg liath.

patterns.title: Tá ... orm
patterns.question: Cad é an focal beag a thaispeánann cé atá tinn? Cad é a tharlaíonn dó nuair a athraíonn an duine?
patterns.questionEn: Which little word tells you who is ill? What happens to it when the person changes?
patterns.rule: In Irish an illness is on you: Tá slaghdán orm (a cold is on me). The person is shown by ar: orm (me), ort (you), air (him), uirthi (her). Ask with An bhfuil ... ort? and answer Tá or Níl.
patterns.ruleEn: In Irish an illness is on you: Tá slaghdán orm (a cold is on me). The person is shown by ar: orm (me), ort (you), air (him), uirthi (her). Ask with An bhfuil ... ort? and answer Tá or Níl.

patterns.title: Ghortaigh mé mo ...
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don fhocal i ndiaidh mo? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn lámh ná rúitín?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the word after mo? Why do lámh and rúitín not change?
patterns.rule: Mo puts a h after the first letter (séimhiú): mo chos, mo ghlúin. L, n and r never take h: mo lámh, mo rúitín. Sc, sm, sp and st do not take h either: mo sceadamán. Before a vowel, mo becomes m': m'uillinn.
patterns.ruleEn: Mo puts a h after the first letter (séimhiú): mo chos, mo ghlúin. L, n and r never take h: mo lámh, mo rúitín. Sc, sm, sp and st do not take h either: mo sceadamán. Before a vowel, mo becomes m': m'uillinn.

ladder.en: I broke my hand. I went to the doctor.
ladder.label: Bunúsach

ladder.ga: Bhris mé mo lámh [ag imirt peile Dé Sathairn seo caite]. Chuaigh mé chuig an dochtúir [san Iúr le mo mhamaí].
ladder.en: I broke my hand playing football last Saturday. I went to the doctor in Newry with my mum.
ladder.label: Níos fearr

ladder.ga: Bhris mé mo lámh ag imirt peile Dé Sathairn seo caite. Chuaigh mé chuig an dochtúir san Iúr le mo mhamaí. [Ar an drochuair, bhí orm scíth a ligean ar feadh seachtaine agus ní raibh cead agam peil a imirt ar feadh míosa. Caithfidh mé a rá gur chuir sé isteach go mór orm, ach beidh mé ar ais ar an fhoireann go luath.]
ladder.en: I broke my hand playing football last Saturday. I went to the doctor in Newry with my mum. Unfortunately, I had to rest for a week and I was not allowed to play football for a month. I have to say that it really annoyed me, but I will be back on the team soon.
ladder.label: Is fearr

roleplays.title: Ag an dochtúir
roleplays.rubric: Tá tú ag an dochtúir san Iúr. Labhraíonn an dochtúir ar dtús.
roleplays.rubricEn: You are at the doctor's in Newry. The doctor speaks first.

tasks.teacher: Dia duit. Cad é atá cearr leat?
tasks.en: Say you have a headache and a sore throat.
tasks.ga: Tá tinneas cinn orm agus tá mo sceadamán nimhneach.

tasks.teacher: Cá fhad atá tú mar seo?
tasks.en: Say for the last two days.
tasks.ga: Le dhá lá anuas.
tasks.alt: Tá mé mar seo le dhá lá anuas.

tasks.teacher: An bhfuil tú ag ithe go maith?
tasks.en: Say you are not hungry but you are drinking a lot of water.
tasks.ga: Níl ocras orm, ach tá mé ag ól a lán uisce.

tasks.teacher: Ceart go leor.
tasks.en: Ask if there is anything that would help you.
tasks.ga: An bhfuil rud ar bith agat a chuideodh liom?

tasks.teacher: Glac dhá tháibléad trí huaire sa lá. An bhfuil teocht ard ort?
tasks.en: Answer the unexpected question.
tasks.ga: Níl, ní shílim go bhfuil.

roleplays.title: Timpiste ag an traenáil
roleplays.rubric: Ghortaigh tú thú féin ag traenáil peile i gCamloch. Tá tú ag caint leis an traenálaí. Labhraíonn an traenálaí ar dtús.
roleplays.rubricEn: You hurt yourself at football training in Camlough. You are talking to the coach. The coach speaks first.

tasks.teacher: Cad é a tharla duit?
tasks.en: Say you fell and hurt your ankle.
tasks.ga: Thit mé agus ghortaigh mé mo mhurnán.
tasks.alt: Thit mé agus ghortaigh mé mo rúitín.

tasks.teacher: An bhfuil sé nimhneach?
tasks.en: Say it is very sore and you cannot walk.
tasks.ga: Tá sé an-nimhneach agus ní thig liom siúl.

tasks.teacher: Cuirfidh mé scairt ar do thuismitheoirí. Cá bhfuil siad inniu?
tasks.en: Say your mum is at work in Newry.
tasks.ga: Tá mo mhamaí ag obair san Iúr.

tasks.teacher: Ceart go leor. Suigh síos anseo go fóill.
tasks.en: Ask for a bottle of water.
tasks.ga: An dtig liom buidéal uisce a fháil, le do thoil?

tasks.teacher: Seo duit. An mbeidh tú ar ais ag an traenáil an tseachtain seo chugainn?
tasks.en: Answer the unexpected question.
tasks.ga: Tá súil agam go mbeidh, ach caithfidh mé dul chuig an dochtúir ar dtús.
